A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated the potential of using resistance pseudogene prevalence to monitor antibiotic use, and we have identified novel resistance mechanisms that may be associated with antibiotic use in cattle.

the presence of antibiotic-resistant bacterial populations in the absence of antibiotic use is not necessarily an indication of high antibiotic use, and the presence of antibiotic resistance genes in bacterial populations growing in an antibiotic use environment is not necessarily a reflection of the level of exposure to those specific antibiotics.
the prevalence of dysfunctional genes and the presence of novel genes are both associated with the level of antibiotic use in the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
resistance gene microarrays can be used to discover new resistance mechanisms and to identify environments where antibiotic use is high.
the prevalence of resistance pseudogenes can be used as a measure of the antibiotic use history of the environment from which E. coli isolations are made.
